title: Parliament passes the Finance (Income Taxes) Bill 2026: US-parented groups exempted from Singapore's MTT, DTT unchanged
summary: Second Minister for Finance Jeffrey Siow moved the second reading of Bill No. 22/2026 on 6 October 2026 and Parliament passed it the same day. Clauses 38 and 49(b) give effect to the Side-by-Side package: US multinational enterprises are exempted from Singapore's Multinational Enterprise Top-up Tax (IIR), while the Domestic Top-up Tax continues to apply to all MNEs in Singapore, including US groups. Under the Bill as tabled, those clauses are deemed to operate from 1 January 2026. Other clauses (36, 37, 39 to 50) align the MMT Act with further international updates, including exchange of GloBE Information Returns so groups only need to file the GIR in one jurisdiction. The Act still needs presidential assent and gazetting, and the detailed safe harbour rules are to follow in regulations.
sourceName: MOF Singapore – Second Reading Opening Speech on the Finance (Income Taxes) Bill, 6 Oct 2026
secondarySourceName: CNA, 'Parliament in brief' 6 Oct 2026 (secondary, confirms passage)
impactNote: Rule-pack review needed: the SG pack still describes the SbS Safe Harbour and the Finance (Income Taxes) Bill as pending/announced. DTT (QDMTT) routing is unchanged. Whether to model the MTT exemption for US-parented groups from FY2026 is a reviewer decision. Do not edit rules or calc without sign-off.

title: Inclusive Framework releases September 2026 Administrative Guidance (Explicitly Conditional Taxes; QDMTT local accounts with mismatched periods)
summary: New Administrative Guidance says an 'Explicitly Conditional Tax' (one that only bites when a Qualified IIR/UTPR applies, or switches off under the Side-by-Side Safe Harbour) is not a Covered Tax, and a DMTT with that feature cannot be a QDMTT. It also clarifies that a QDMTT can still use local financial accounting standards for the QDMTT Safe Harbour where a local entity's accounting period differs from the UPE's year, provided the same period is used for that entity in the consolidated accounts. The document was approved by the Inclusive Framework on 2 September 2026 and published on 11 September 2026.
sourceName: OECD – Administrative Guidance on the GloBE Model Rules, September 2026 (PDF)
impactNote: No engine parameter changes. Covered-taxes input should exclude any Explicitly Conditional Tax; add input guidance.

title: Updated GloBE Information Return (September 2026) incorporates the Side-by-Side Package
summary: The OECD published a revised GIR that adds data points and elections for the Side-by-Side, Simplified ETR, Substance-based Tax Incentive and UPE safe harbours, plus new reporting on government-provided benefits. The revised template is only for Fiscal Years commencing on or after 31 December 2025, but new explanatory notes on existing data points apply to future filings for earlier years too. A revised GIR XML Schema was still to follow.
impactNote: none (projection only). Domestic filing deadlines in the packs are unchanged.
verificationNote: OECD page blocks automated fetch (bot check); date and abstract confirmed from the OECD page text in the search index and the full EY alert.

title: Terms of Reference and Assessment Methodology for the Full Legislative Review published
summary: The Inclusive Framework set out how it will run full peer reviews of jurisdictions' IIR, UTPR and DMTT legislation, which go beyond the transitional qualification mechanism. Outcomes, including any prospective loss of qualified status, will be recorded in the OECD Central Record. Approved by the Inclusive Framework on 2 September 2026 and published with the September package.
sourceName: OECD – Terms of Reference and Assessment Methodology for the Full Legislative Review (PDF)
impactNote: Watch item: a future loss of qualified status for HK/SG/JP would change hasQdmtt in the packs.

title: Second ratification triggers entry into force of the STTR Multilateral Convention on 1 January 2027
summary: Albania deposited its instrument of ratification of the Subject to Tax Rule (STTR) Multilateral Convention on 15 September 2026, the second after San Marino. That satisfies the entry-into-force condition, so the Convention enters into force on 1 January 2027 as a formal matter. No tax treaty is yet covered, so practical impact is currently limited.
impactNote: none. STTR is treaty-based and not modelled.
verificationNote: Secondary source only. The OECD depositary page was not fetched.

title: Finance (Income Taxes) Bill 2026 tabled, amending the MMT Act for the Side-by-Side Safe Harbour and GIR exchange
summary: Bill No. 22/2026 was read the first time on 8 September 2026. Besides Budget 2026 income tax changes, it amends the Multinational Enterprise (Minimum Tax) Act 2024 to support the Side-by-Side Safe Harbour (to be detailed in regulations, by reference to the OECD webpage listing qualified SbS regimes), the GIR exchange framework under the GIR MCAA, and powers to exempt MTT/DTT return filing. It also lets regulations prescribe when a Singapore entity's FANIL for DTT is its own financial-statement net income.
sourceName: Singapore Statutes Online – Finance (Income Taxes) Bill (Bill No. 22/2026)
impactNote: DTT (QDMTT) routing unchanged. The SbS safe harbour (MTT/IIR side, FY2026+) is not modelled; track the Bill's passage.

dateNote: The document is labelled 'September 2026 update' (令和8年9月更新) without a day. The date shown is the PDF creation date (14 Sep 2026); the server's last-modified date was 24 Sep 2026.
title: NTA e-Tax updates GIR XML/CSV recording guidelines (September 2026)
summary: The NTA's e-Tax 'Multinational Enterprise Information Reporting Corner' page now carries September 2026 updates to the GIR recording guidelines (XML/CSV) and the Excel-to-CSV procedure. The page says the guidelines were revised to reflect the Inclusive Framework's June 2026 guidance on using the GIR XML Schema and validation rules for first GIR filings and exchanges.
sourceName: NTA e-Tax – 多国籍企業情報の報告コーナーについて

title: NTA releases amended administrative guidance and Q&As for Japanese IIR, UTPR and QDMTT
summary: The NTA issued amended administrative guidance (Japanese only) reflecting the 2026 tax reform, plus revised IIR Q&As and a new Q&A set covering the UTPR and QDMTT that apply to fiscal years beginning on or after 1 April 2026. A special measure lets jurisdictional adjusted covered taxes include a special tax-credit-equivalent amount for the IIR from fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2026.
sourceName: KPMG Japan e-Tax News No.357, 17 Aug 2026
impactNote: none for v0.2. Confirms the 1 April 2026 QDMTT/UTPR start already in jp.v1.
verificationNote: Date and scope confirmed from KPMG Japan. Special-measure detail per KPMG US TaxNewsFlash (17 Aug 2026) and the MOF FY2026 outline. NTA Japanese originals not reviewed line by line.

title: Central Record updated (current as at 1 May 2026): HK, SG and JP listed
summary: The Central Record approved on 11 May 2026 lists Hong Kong and Singapore with transitional qualified status for their IIR and QDMTT (with QDMTT Safe Harbour) from 1 January 2025. Japan's IIR is listed from 1 April 2024, and its QDMTT (with QDMTT Safe Harbour) from 1 April 2026.
sourceName: OECD – Updated Central Record for Purposes of the Global Minimum Tax (PDF)
impactNote: Source for the qualified-status fields and QDMTT effective dates that drive hasQdmtt in hk/sg/jp.v1.

title: MOF publishes responses to consultation on the proposed Finance (Income Taxes) Bill 2026
summary: MOF had consulted on the draft Bill from 8 June to 1 July 2026 and published its summary of responses on 2 September 2026, ahead of tabling the Bill on 8 September.

title: IRD publishes GIR XML Schema, user guides and opens test GIR submissions on the Pillar Two Portal
summary: IRD updated its global minimum tax webpage with the OECD GIR XML Schema, the OECD user guide and an IRD supplementary user guide for preparing a GIR. Part 4AA entities can now submit test GIR data files to the Pillar Two Portal for validation.

title: Hong Kong signs the GIR Multilateral Competent Authority Agreement
summary: Hong Kong signed the GIR MCAA, a qualifying competent authority agreement under the GloBE rules. In-scope groups can now make a central GloBE filing in or outside Hong Kong, and rely on exchange instead of filing the GIR section locally.
sourceName: IRD – Global minimum tax and HKMTT

title: Cabinet approves FY2026 tax reform outline: Side-by-Side exemption, CbCR safe harbour extension
summary: The FY2026 outline gives Japan's IIR a zero-top-up exemption for groups whose UPE is in a jurisdiction designated by the Finance Minister as meeting the Side-by-Side criteria, from fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2026. It extends the transitional CbCR safe harbour by one year to 31 December 2027 (also for the QDMTT), and allows certain qualifying tax-credit amounts to be added to adjusted covered taxes.
sourceName: Ministry of Finance Japan – FY2026 reform outline (global minimum tax)
impactNote: SbS exemption affects the IIR only. QDMTT routing unchanged; not modelled in v0.2.

title: IRD launches Phase 1 of the Pillar Two Portal for top-up tax notifications
summary: Phase 1 of the Pillar Two Portal opened on 19 January 2026 for filing annual top-up tax notifications. Phase 2, for top-up tax returns and electronic assessment notices, is stated for Q4 2026.
sourceName: IRD – Global minimum tax and HKMTT

title: Inclusive Framework agrees the Side-by-Side package
summary: The package includes a Simplified ETR Safe Harbour, an extension of the Transitional CbCR Safe Harbour, a Substance-based Tax Incentive Safe Harbour, and a Side-by-Side system made up of a Side-by-Side Safe Harbour and a UPE Safe Harbour.
sourceName: IRAS – GloBE Rules and DTT (describes the IF agreement of 5 Jan 2026)
impactNote: Safe-harbour logic is Phase 3 scope. The current safe harbour flag is a manual boolean.
verificationNote: OECD original not fetched (bot check). Official IRAS page used as the source.

title: Inland Revenue (Amendment) (Minimum Tax for Multinational Enterprise Groups) Ordinance 2025 enacted
summary: Ordinance No. 21 of 2025 adds Part 4AA and Schedules 61–64 to the Inland Revenue Ordinance, implementing the IIR and the HKMTT for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2025. The UTPR starts on a date the Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury will specify by Gazette notice.
sourceName: IRD – Global minimum tax and HKMTT
impactNote: Basis for HK: HKMTT and IIR from FY beginning on/after 1 Jan 2025 (hk.v1).
verificationNote: IRD states the Ordinance was enacted on 6 June 2025. The Gazette copy shows the Chief Executive's signature dated 5 June 2025 and commencement on publication in the Gazette.
